priorityLevels.meaning: Blocking security, data-integrity, financial-correctness, authorization, critical-journey or required recovery control.
priorityLevels.releaseRule: Must be implemented and have passing evidence before enabling affected critical/LIVE behavior. An accepted-risk note cannot silently waive a mandatory P0.
priorityLevels.exceptionRule: If an integration/feature is conditional, keep it disabled behind a server-controlled feature gate until required controls pass; this is not the same as marking the control passed.

priorityLevels.meaning: Important reliability, monitoring, usability, auditability or secondary hardening requirement.
priorityLevels.releaseRule: Complete before general rollout or the specific feature’s release gate; if not complete, document impact, owner, compensating controls and target date.
priorityLevels.exceptionRule: Risk acceptance must be explicit, bounded, owned and reviewed; it must not weaken legal/security obligations or bypass a mandatory P0.

priorityLevels.meaning: Optional/future improvement where the approved scope explicitly permits deferral.
priorityLevels.releaseRule: May be scheduled after P0/P1 according to product scope; never reclassify a security P0 as P2 merely to ship.
priorityLevels.exceptionRule: Must have a recorded scope decision and owner; no untracked downgrade.
examples: non-blocking visual polish or optional diagnostics not required by an acceptance criterion

conditionalPriorityRules.meaning: For an optional provider/integration, controls are mandatory before the integration can be enabled; until then it must remain disabled and unreachable through client-controlled flags.
A critical P0 failure blocks the relevant release or feature; the failure cannot be relabelled PASS through a waiver.
P1 may only be deferred through an approved, bounded risk record and must not undermine any P0 guardrail.

statusSemantics.meaning: Work has started, not yet accepted.
A dependency/decision prevents the step from completing.
Per project execution policy, the step is deferred to the consolidated final-review list; this is not acceptance, closure or test pass.
Acceptance criteria met with traceable test/build evidence, build/version/environment recorded.
Acceptance criteria not met; corrective work required.
Explicit, owned, time-bounded risk record; cannot auto-override mandatory P0 controls.

separationRules: Security requirement P0/P1 priority is separate from UI screen P0/P1/P2 priority; one cannot change the other.
A baseline initial status VERIFY, implementation status UNVERIFIED, NOT_RUN test or static source match is not a PASS.
Skipped for final review means deferred discussion/testing, not that the requirement is complete.
Feature flags and client-side labels do not replace server-side authorization or environment gates.
Any exception requires a risk ID, owner, rationale, compensating controls, approval authority, expiry/review date and verification evidence.

controls: fresh authentication and purpose-bound OTP when required by action policy

enforcementRules: Risk level is enforced by Backend handlers; hiding UI buttons is not a security control.
Missing required permission, verification or approval blocks the operation.
Audit should capture actor, target, timestamp, outcome, request ID and applicable before/after values.
Downgrading risk or weakening controls requires an authorized, audited configuration change.
The action-by-action risk map must be reconciled against actual Admin screens, endpoint handlers, permissions and the 67 security requirements.
